options: Connects the two bones of the leg to the talus
Is a ball-and-socket joint
Connects the talus to the calcaneus
Is a diarthrosis of the ginglymus (hinge) type
Is a recessed (mortise) joint ensuring the stability of the foot during walking and running
questions.explanation: The talocrural joint is a ginglymus uniting tibia and fibula to the talus. The talus–calcaneus joint is the subtalar joint.

questions.stem: Which of the following are tarsal joints?
options: The tarsometatarsal joints
The talocrural joint
The transverse joint of the foot
The joints of the distal tarsal bones with each other
The subtalar joint
questions.explanation: Tarsometatarsal joints belong to the forefoot; the talocrural joint is its own class.

questions.stem: The tibiofibular articular surfaces of the ankle are formed by:
options: The articular facet of the lateral malleolus
The inferior articular surface of the tibia
The head of the fibula
The articular facet of the medial malleolus
The tibial plateau
questions.explanation: These three surfaces form the mortise receiving the trochlea of the talus.

options: Is a large articular projection
Its lateral malleolar surface is comma-shaped
Its medial malleolar surface is triangular
Its upper surface articulates with the fibula
Its upper surface articulates with the inferior surface of the tibia
questions.explanation: Medial malleolar surface = comma-shaped; lateral malleolar surface = triangular. Also false: "Its medial malleolar surface is triangular"; "Its upper surface articulates with the fibula".

questions.stem: How are the articular surfaces of the talocrural joint organized?
options: The talar trochlea forms a mortise receiving the malleoli
The tibiofibular surfaces form a mortise into which the talar trochlea fits
The calcaneus forms the floor of the mortise
The navicular closes the mortise in front
The fibula alone forms the superior wall
questions.explanation: Tibia (inferior surface, medial malleolus) and fibula (lateral malleolus) form the mortise for the talar trochlea.

questions.stem: The medial (deltoid) ligament of the ankle:
options: Is strong and triangular
Has a deep layer with tibionavicular and tibiocalcaneal bundles
Has its apex attached to the medial malleolus
Is the ligament typically injured in ankle sprains
Has a superficial layer with anterior and posterior tibiotalar bundles
questions.explanation: The lateral ligament is "the ankle sprain ligament". Also false: "Has a superficial layer with anterior and posterior tibiotalar bundles"; "Has a deep layer with tibionavicular and tibiocalcaneal bundles".

questions.stem: The lateral ligament of the ankle:
options: Extends from the lateral malleolus
Includes the tibionavicular bundle
Is called "the ankle sprain ligament"
Is the strongest ligament of the ankle
Ends in two bundles
questions.explanation: The strong, triangular ligament is the medial (deltoid) ligament. Also false: "Ends in two bundles"; "Includes the tibionavicular bundle".

questions.stem: A basketball player twists their foot inward and has pain below the lateral malleolus. Which ligament is most likely injured?
options: The tibionavicular bundle
The deltoid ligament
The anterior cruciate ligament
The lateral ligament of the ankle
The tibial collateral ligament
questions.explanation: The lateral ligament (anterior talofibular, calcaneofibular, posterior talofibular) is the ligament of common ankle sprains.

questions.stem: Which bundles belong to the deep layer of the deltoid ligament?
options: The posterior tibiotalar bundle
The calcaneofibular bundle
The tibionavicular bundle
The anterior tibiotalar bundle
The tibiocalcaneal bundle
questions.explanation: Deep layer: anterior and posterior tibiotalar. Superficial: tibionavicular and tibiocalcaneal. Calcaneofibular belongs to the lateral ligament.

questions.stem: The synovium of the talocrural joint:
options: Forms a cul-de-sac extension between the tibia and the fibula
Covers the articular cartilage
Is continuous with the knee synovium
Forms the quadriceps recess
Lines the inner surface of the capsule
questions.explanation: It lines the capsule and sends a recess between tibia and fibula. The quadriceps recess belongs to the knee.

questions.stem: About the movements of the talocrural joint:
options: Extension (plantar flexion) has an amplitude of 30° to 60°
Movements occur around a vertical axis
Flexion has an amplitude of 30° to 60°
Flexion (dorsiflexion) brings the dorsum of the foot toward the front of the leg
It has three degrees of freedom
questions.explanation: Flexion-extension occur around a transverse axis. Also false: "It has three degrees of freedom"; "Flexion has an amplitude of 30° to 60°".

questions.stem: What is the amplitude of extension (plantar flexion) of the ankle?
Dorsiflexion of the foot is also called:
options: Extension
Flexion
Lowering
Plantar flexion
Elevation
questions.explanation: Flexion = dorsiflexion = elevation; extension = plantar flexion = lowering.
